Construction intelligence · connected operations

One operating context for the job.

NEXUS connects people, project information, BIM, specialist tools and field execution so the right information reaches the right person without breaking project memory.

Work Zone

A focused work environment that presents only the tools, tasks, documents, contacts and project information relevant to the work being done.

Shared project cloud

Managers, site teams and office users work from the same live project context, reducing manual re-entry and fragmented information.

Instant information flow

A task can arrive with drawings, location, checklist, contacts and evidence requirements already attached.

BIM + FAB

Model intelligence meets real-world execution.

BIM provides structured building context. Fabrication technologies turn model information into manufacturable work. NEXUS connects both to people, tasks, QA, delivery and long-term project memory.

BIM / Digital Twin

Architectural, structural and MEP models become operational context rather than isolated files. Model elements can be associated with documents, tasks, people, inspections, evidence and asset history.

DoorFlow

Plan → Schedule → Match → Install → Evidence → Sign-off

DoorFlow is the first practical NEXUS execution pattern: floor plans, door schedules, installation status, snag photos and sign-off evidence connected in one live fit-out layer.

Plan matching

Match door references from drawings with the schedule and floor context.

Status layer

Show not started, in progress, complete, blocked or requiring evidence.

Evidence loop

Attach photos, notes, snags and sign-off actions to the correct door ID.

DoorFlow is not only about doors. The same execution pattern can extend into fire stopping, M&E assets, joinery packages, snagging, inspections and handover evidence.

Circular manufacturing / ecology

GreenLoop.

NOSMO GreenLoop is focused on converting selected automotive plastic waste into recycled natural-fibre composite material, practical prototypes and future high-strength printed products.

SourceSortShredDryBlendPrint
Feedstock

Automotive plastic parts

Clean, identifiable, controlled plastic streams with supplier traceability, batch notes and photos.

Material

Natural-fibre composite

Recycled base polymer combined with chopped hemp fibre or other reinforcement where appropriate, developed through pellets, filament and test coupons.

Evidence

Working prototypes

Useful printed parts, sample products, fixtures and test components supported by material and manufacturing records.

Hemp fibre track

Ecology first. Strength where it matters.

A longer-term GreenLoop direction is controlled placement of natural hemp fibre inside recycled polymer to produce stronger bio-composite printed parts than ordinary plastic printing.

What we want to explore

A multi-axis printer or robotic cell can lay reinforcement along structural load paths instead of only printing flat layers.

In simple terms: print the recycled plastic body and lace natural fibre through it where stiffness and strength are needed.

Engineering reality

Hemp fibre is ecological and cost-effective but requires careful drying, fibre treatment, polymer compatibility testing, mechanical testing, water absorption testing, weathering checks and layer-bond validation.
